subject: clean-label concept
object: clean labels omit perceived undesirable ingredients and may display natural claims but need not be additive-free and have no exact universal definition
quotes: A clean label is a label on a food, not listing ingredients that may be perceived by consumers as undesirable.
It does not necessarily mean that the product is free from additives
There is no exact definition of which ingredients precisely may be included or excluded in a clean label.
accepted: The clean-label page describes omitting ingredients perceived as undesirable and displaying natural or no-artificial claims, but says this need not mean additive-free and has no exact included-or-excluded ingredient definition. It is general marketing and formulation context, not an audit or a health or safety result for an exact offer.

subject: monosodium glutamate
object: MSG is the sodium salt of glutamic acid and can enhance savory or umami perception
quotes: Monosodium glutamate ( MSG ), also known as sodium glutamate ,  is a sodium salt of glutamic acid .
MSG is used in cooking as a flavor enhancer with a savory taste that intensifies the umami flavor of food
MSG balances, blends, and rounds the perception of other tastes.
accepted: The MSG page identifies monosodium glutamate as the sodium salt of glutamic acid and describes a savory or umami flavor-enhancing function. These are identity and flavor-mechanism facts only; they do not establish an exact snack formula, amount, exposure, child-specific outcome, medical conclusion or product safety ranking.

subject: glutamate flavoring
object: glutamic acid and glutamates occur in aged foods and yeast extract and the flavor-relevant ion can arise from different starting compounds
quotes: Glutamic acid and glutamates are natural constituents of many fermented or aged foods
They can also be found in hydrolyzed proteins such as yeast extract .
Only the glutamate ion is responsible for the umami flavor, so the effect does not depend significantly on the starting compound.
accepted: The glutamate-flavoring page says glutamic acid and glutamates occur in fermented or aged foods and hydrolyzed proteins such as yeast extract, and that the flavor-relevant glutamate ion can arise from different starting compounds. This distinguishes broader glutamate flavoring from MSG without adjudicating an exact no-MSG claim or proving a health or safety result.

subject: food additives
object: additives can preserve or alter sensory qualities, may have natural or artificial origins and can have overlapping functions
quotes: Food additives are substances added to food to preserve flavor or enhance taste, appearance, or other sensory qualities.
many additives having both natural and artificial origin were introduced.
Food additives can be divided into several groups, although there is some overlap because some additives exert more than one effect.
accepted: The food-additive page describes preservation and sensory functions, natural and artificial origins, and category overlap. A claim excluding one additive class does not disclose an exact complete formula or establish that a whole product is additive-free, healthier, safer or better.

subject: food coloring
object: a colorant imparts color, may be natural or synthesized, and can offset loss, stabilize variation or identify flavor
quotes: Food coloring , color additive or colorant is any dye , pigment , or substance that imparts color when it is added to food or beverages.
Some colorings may be natural
or may be synthesized
accepted: The food-coloring page defines a colorant as a substance that imparts color and notes that colorings may be natural or synthesized and serve several appearance functions. Source class and function do not reveal an exact snack formula or automatically rank whole-product quality, health or safety.

subject: food flavoring
object: flavorings improve taste or smell and nature-identical compounds can be chemically equivalent to natural compounds while synthesized
quotes: A flavoring (or flavouring ), [ a ] also known as flavor (or flavour ) or flavorant , is a food additive that is used to improve the taste or smell of food.

most commercial flavorings are "nature-identical", which means that they are the chemical equivalent of natural flavors, but chemically synthesized rather than having been extracted from source materials.
accepted: The flavoring page defines flavorings by taste or smell function and describes nature-identical compounds as chemically equivalent to natural flavors while synthesized. These classifications do not identify an exact formula or make natural, artificial or nature-identical flavoring an automatic health, safety or quality rank.

subject: natural-food labeling
object: natural and all-natural are marketing terms with several definitions and consumer assumptions that vary by context
quotes: Natural food and all-natural food are terms in food labeling and marketing with several definitions
Not to be confused with whole food .
The term is variously misused on labels and in advertisements.
accepted: The natural-food page calls natural and all-natural labeling and marketing terms with several definitions, distinguishes the topic from whole food, and says the term is variously misused. This frozen background does not audit current law or an exact label and does not make natural synonymous with organic, healthy or safe.

quotes: TIL MSG occurs naturally in tomatoes and other vegetables.
Naturally occurring doesn't signify anything.
Just because a chemical can be found in food we consume doesn't mean anything besides we have allowed it to remain.
accepted: The community thread title says MSG occurs naturally in tomatoes and vegetables, while a reply says natural occurrence alone signifies nothing. This is scoped debate about naturalness rhetoric, not an authoritative exact-formula audit, medical conclusion or safety result.

subject: MSG ELI5 community thread
object: participants offer conflicting explanations of MSG taste, public fear, yeast extract, sodium and alleged outcomes
quotes: ELI5: Why does MSG make food taste so irresistible? And why is everyone against it?
MSG contains glutamic acid, which is what causes things to taste savory, a flavor known as "umami."
That doesn't sound very plausible. When MSG dissolves, it dissociates into sodium ions and glutamate ions.
accepted: The MSG ELI5 thread contains competing community explanations about umami, sodium, yeast extract, public fear and alleged health effects. It can identify beliefs and questions to check, but cannot serve as authoritative chemistry, medicine, exact product formula, exposure or safety evidence.

subject: whole-wheat ELI5 community thread
object: participants argue that a front claim may not disclose proportions and recommend checking ingredient and nutrition details
quotes: ELI5: What do food product labels that say “whole wheat” or “100% whole grain wheat” mean? Are these better for health?
Reading the ingredients/nutritional facts is the only way to determine "health."
the front of the package is to lure you, the back is to inform you.
accepted: The whole-wheat community thread debates front-label wording versus ingredient and nutrition details. It motivates auditing complete exact labels rather than inferring composition from a prominent phrase, but it is not current legal advice, a clean-label definition or evidence about the five snack formulas.

subject: child-snack visualization discussion
object: comments describe 1,135 online parent responses with at least about twenty per state and criticize sampling, self-report, outliers and missing intervals
quotes: This presents on-line survey data of parents about the sweet foods their children consume, n = 1,135, with a minimum of n = 20 per state.
People who answer on-line surveys are not a representative sample of parents in the United States.
accepted: The visualization discussion describes online self-report from 1,135 parents with a minimum of about twenty per state and criticizes representativeness, outliers and missing uncertainty. It is a scoped method critique, not a validated state ranking, child consumption estimate or evidence about an exact household.
